title: What's in Spend?
summary: Check what you have before you buy, and work out what's left.

steps.title: Spend is the cash you hold
steps.body: Before you buy something, check what's in Spend. If the price is the same or less, you can pay. What you have minus the price is what's left.
steps.example: You have {m:1200} in Spend. A book costs {m:750}. After buying it you have {m:450} left.

steps.prompt: You have {m:900} in Spend. Which one can you buy today?

options.feedback: Not quite. {m:1500} is more than the {m:900} you have.
Not quite. {m:2000} is more than double what you have.

hints: Only one price is smaller than {m:900}.
steps.correct: Nice. That's it. The comic fits inside what you have.

replay.prompt: You have {m:1100} in Spend. Which one can you buy today?

options.feedback: Not quite. {m:2500} is far more than {m:1100}.

replay.correct: Nice. That's it. The puzzle fits inside what you have.

steps.prompt: You have {m:1500} in Spend. You buy a hat for {m:900}. How much is left?

misconceptions.feedback: That adds the two amounts. Buying takes money away.
That's the price of the hat. What's left after paying it?

steps.wrong: Not quite. Take the price away from what you have.
hints: Start with {m:1500} and take away the price.
steps.correct: That's it. {m:600} is left in Spend.

replay.prompt: You have {m:2000} in Spend. You buy socks for {m:450}. How much is left?

misconceptions.feedback: That adds the two amounts. Buying takes money away.
That's the price of the socks. What's left after paying it?

replay.wrong: Not quite. Take the price away from what you have.
hints: Start with {m:2000} and take away the price.
replay.correct: That's it. {m:1550} is left in Spend.

steps.prompt: You have {m:800}. You buy a snack for {m:300}. Can you still buy a {m:600} ticket?

options.feedback: Not quite. Check what's left after the snack first.

steps.outcome: After the snack you have {m:500}. The ticket costs {m:600}, so you'd be {m:100} short. Each buy changes what's left for the next one.
hints: Work out what's left after the snack.
{m:800} take away {m:300} is {m:500}. Is that enough for {m:600}?
steps.correct: Right. The snack leaves {m:500}, which is less than {m:600}.

steps.prompt: You have {m:1000} in Spend. Could you buy each one on its own?
steps.wrong: One of them is in the wrong group. A price the same as what you have still fits.
hints: A price of exactly {m:1000} still fits.
steps.correct: All sorted. Anything up to {m:1000} fits on its own.

steps.prompt: You have {m:1200}. Sticker packs cost {m:300} each. How many packs can you buy?

misconceptions.feedback: Three packs cost {m:900}. You'd still have {m:300}, enough for one more.
Five packs would cost {m:1500}. That's more than you have.

steps.wrong: Not quite. See how many times {m:300} fits into {m:1200}.
hints: Add {m:300} at a time until you reach {m:1200}.
steps.correct: That's it. Four packs cost exactly {m:1200}.

replay.prompt: You have {m:1500}. Sticker packs cost {m:400} each. How many packs can you buy?

misconceptions.feedback: Four packs would cost {m:1600}. That's more than you have.
Two packs cost {m:800}. There's enough left for one more.

replay.wrong: Not quite. See how many times {m:400} fits into {m:1500}.
hints: Add {m:400} at a time without going over {m:1500}.
replay.correct: That's it. Three packs cost {m:1200}, and {m:300} is left over.

steps.prompt: Why is it worth checking Spend before you buy?

options.text: So you know you can pay and what will be left

options.feedback: Prices can change, but that isn't the reason. Think about what you have.

options.text: So you can spend all of it at once
options.feedback: Not quite. Checking helps you decide, not spend everything.

hints: Checking shows whether the price fits and what you'd have after.
steps.correct: Right. Checking first means no surprises at the till.
